final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with three core pillars: (1) 75% auto RVC + wage-floor enforcement via joint audits with automatic remedy suspension, (2) 3.6% Canadian dairy market access effective year one, and (3) Article 34 auto-renewal presumption with 18-month objection window and opt-in renegotiation trigger. USTR set a 2 PM same-day drafting deadline to lock legal text and close the deal.
minority_objections: Canada initially resisted auto-renewal without renegotiation rights, proposing mandatory good-faith renegotiation window before renewal takes effect
Supply-chain manufacturers raised unresolved concerns about audit cost allocation and supplier cure windows before suspension
key_conflicts: Canada vs. USTR on Article 34 renewal language: Canada wanted objection to trigger renegotiation; USTR demanded auto-renewal with opt-in amendments only
Congress vs. USTR on enforcement specificity: Congress demanded facility-level remedy triggers and tariff-line suspension details in legal text, not framework language
Auto industry vs. Mexico on audit mechanics: who pays for inspections and whether suppliers get cure window before market-access suspension
key_concessions: Canada accepted 3.6% dairy market access (cheese, butter, yogurt combined) effective year one with no phase-in
USTR accepted presumption-of-renewal language with 18-month objection window instead of hard five-year sunset
Mexico accepted joint-audit framework with 60-day timelines, majority-vote violation findings, and automatic remedy suspension
Canada accepted auto-renewal presumption in exchange for opt-in renegotiation trigger language
red_lines: USTR: no renegotiation-from-scratch language at year five that would create investment uncertainty for Congress
Canada: no hard sunset without review mechanism; objection must preserve renegotiation rights
Congress: labor enforcement must include automatic facility-level remedy suspension, not dispute-panel delays
Dairy industry: 3.6% market access must be in Article 34 legal text by 2 PM deadline, not separate negotiation
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Audit cost allocation and supplier cure-window mechanics left unresolved despite repeated questions from auto industry and supply-chain manufacturers
Whether violation at one supplier blocks entire producer's benefits or just that product line remained ambiguous
Dispute settlement (Chapter 19) never surfaced despite being a known Canadian priority in historical context
Steel/aluminum tariff linkage to USMCA package not discussed despite being active U.S. leverage at this date
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification depends on seeing both Article 34 renewal text AND labor enforcement remedy details in same legal draft by 2 PM
Canadian parliamentary ratification risk if dairy concession (3.6%) triggers domestic backlash from supply-management lobby
Supply-chain investment decisions frozen until audit-cost and cure-window details finalized in legal text
Mexico's sovereignty concerns if joint-audit framework interpreted as allowing unilateral U.S. facility inspections
uncertainty_notes: Legal text drafting deadline set for 2 PM same day, but multiple enforcement details unresolved: audit cost-sharing, supplier cure windows, product-line vs. producer-level suspension scope. Dairy market-access percentage (3.6%) agreed in principle but unclear if it appears in Article 34 text or separate agricultural annex. Canada's opt-in renegotiation trigger language not yet drafted. USTR threatened to proceed with Mexico-only bilateral if Canada did not accept auto-renewal terms by deadline.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC + wage-floor enforcement drove the entire labor-audit framework negotiation; USTR set it as floor Canada must match, and it shaped the joint-audit proposal that became a package pillar
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Congress explicitly demanded facility-level remedy triggers and automatic suspension language in legal text as ratification condition; drove Mexico's 60-day audit + majority-vote + automatic-suspension proposal
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: 3.6% market access became explicit linkage to Article 34 renewal text; dairy industry stated 'no deal if not in 2 PM text' and USTR used it as quid pro quo for Canada joining package
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Never mentioned in transcript; no discussion of Chapter 19 or state-to-state panels
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset explicitly rejected by all parties; drove Article 34 auto-renewal presumption + 18-month objection window compromise that became the deal-closing mechanism
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress repeatedly conditioned ratification on specific legal-text details (enforcement language, renewal clarity); USTR set 2 PM deadline explicitly to secure Congressional votes; shaped final package structure
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers raised audit costs, cure windows, and Mexican capacity-commitment freezes multiple times, but these concerns were acknowledged and deferred to legal-text drafting rather than driving concessions
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: USTR explicitly threatened 'Mexico alone and Canada joins later on our terms' if Canada rejected auto-renewal by 2 PM, but this was late-stage leverage after package already forming, not the driver of Canada's dairy concession
